name: Doha
operatingHours: Doha Metro (Red, Green and Gold lines) runs ~5:00 AM–~1:00 AM Saturday–Thursday and ~9:00 AM–~1:00 AM on Friday; last-train times vary by station. Trains every ~3–6 min by day, less often late evening. The Lusail Tram and Msheireb Tram use the same cards.
fareInfo: Standard Travel Card QR 10 to buy; each journey QR 2, capped at QR 6 per day. Gold Club card QR 100 to buy; QR 10 per journey, capped at QR 30 per day. Metropasses: 7 days QR 40, 30 days QR 120. Cards also cover the Lusail Tram and Metrolink feeder buses. The airport station uses the same fares.

sights.name: Souq Waqif
sights.note: A rebuilt traditional market of mud-rendered lanes selling spices, textiles, perfume and falconry gear, with cafés and restaurants that stay busy late into the night.
sights.hours: Lanes open all day; most shops ~10:00 AM–noon and ~4:00 PM–11:00 PM, restaurants later

sights.name: Museum of Islamic Art
sights.note: I. M. Pei's geometric stone museum on its own island off the Corniche, holding 1,400 years of Islamic art from Spain to Central Asia, with skyline views from the atrium.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–7:00 PM Sat–Tue, to 9:00 PM Thu, 1:30–7:00 PM Fri; closed Wed

sights.name: MIA Park
sights.note: A landscaped waterfront park around the Museum of Islamic Art, with lawns, a crescent promenade, Richard Serra's sculpture 7 and views across the bay to West Bay.

sights.name: The Corniche
sights.note: A 7 km palm-lined seafront promenade curving around Doha Bay between the Museum of Islamic Art and the West Bay towers, popular for evening walks and dhow rides.

sights.name: National Museum of Qatar
sights.note: Jean Nouvel's 'desert rose' building of interlocking discs, telling Qatar's story from geology and Bedouin life to oil, wrapped around the restored palace of Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim.
sights.hours: ~9:00 AM–7:00 PM Sat–Thu, from 1:30 PM Fri

sights.name: Fanar – Qatar Islamic Cultural Center
sights.note: The spiral-minaret mosque and cultural centre beside Souq Waqif, offering visitors free introductions to Islam and Qatari customs.
sights.hours: ~8:00 AM–noon Sun–Thu; visitor tours vary, check ahead

sights.name: Msheireb Museums
sights.note: Four restored heritage houses in the Msheireb quarter covering Doha's early urban life, the pearling-era labour migration and the history of the slave trade in the Gulf.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM Sat–Thu, from 3:00 PM Fri

sights.name: Msheireb Downtown
sights.note: A newly rebuilt car-light city quarter of shaded lanes, cafés and public squares such as Barahat Msheireb, linked by a free loop tram.

sights.name: Old Doha Port
sights.note: The former port turned waterfront district, with brightly painted shipping-container shops and cafés in the Mina District and a marina for cruise ships.
sights.hours: Open streets; shops and cafés ~10:00 AM–late

sights.name: Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab Mosque
sights.note: Qatar's national mosque, a vast sandstone building with 90 domes; non-Muslim visitors are welcome outside prayer times in modest dress.
sights.hours: Visits outside prayer times; closed to visitors Friday midday

sights.name: Museum of Illusions Doha
sights.note: A hands-on museum of optical illusions, tilted rooms and mirror installations on the first floor of The Gate Mall in West Bay.

sights.name: Katara Cultural Village
sights.note: A seafront arts quarter with a Greek-style amphitheatre, galleries, pigeon towers, ornate mosques, a public beach and many restaurants.
sights.hours: Open 24 hours; venues and restaurants ~10:00 AM–midnight

sights.name: The Pearl-Qatar
sights.note: An artificial island of marinas and Mediterranean-style apartment blocks; the Porto Arabia boardwalk and the canal-side Qanat Quartier are the parts to stroll.
sights.hours: Open 24 hours; shops and restaurants ~10:00 AM–late

sights.name: Qatar National Library
sights.note: Rem Koolhaas's library in Education City, a single open hall of terraced white bookshelves around a sunken heritage collection of manuscripts and maps.

sights.name: Aspire Park
sights.note: Doha's largest park, next to the Aspire Tower and Khalifa International Stadium, with a lake, jogging tracks and shaded lawns that fill up on cooler evenings.

sights.name: Khalifa International Stadium
sights.note: The national stadium of Qatar, rebuilt for the 2022 World Cup with a twin-arch roof; the 3-2-1 Qatar Olympic and Sports Museum sits beside it.
sights.hours: Exterior anytime; museum ~9:00 AM–7:00 PM, from 1:30 PM Fri

airports.name: Hamad International Airport
airports.transitNote: Red Line from the HIA T1 station, connected to the terminal, reaches Msheireb in ~20 min and West Bay in ~30 min; the line is on this map. Karwa taxis to the centre take ~20 min.
airports.hours: Red Line at the airport: first train ~5:00 AM (~9:00 AM Fri), last ~midnight; no overnight trains.
